claim: PJM posted TLR Level 5a Action 105558 for flowgate 27750 (Peach Bottom-Conastone 5012 500 kV), effective 18:00 EPT on 2026-10-13. This establishes a transmission-loading-relief action; it does not establish which interchange transactions were curtailed or reallocated, the delivered relief, customer interruption, or backup-generator use.

source.title: PJM Emergency Procedures Postings — Message 105558

source.title: NERC IRO-006-5: Reliability Coordination — Transmission Loading Relief

falsifier: A corrected or withdrawn PJM posting showing Message 105558 was erroneous, a drill, or never became effective would falsify the operational-transition claim. Transaction-level records showing no curtailment or reallocation would not falsify issuance but would falsify any claimed realized relief.
firstUnsupportedArrow: TLR Level 5a issuance -> identified transactions actually curtailed or reallocated -> measured flowgate relief -> avoided escalation or customer consequence
omissions: No transaction identities, priorities, megawatts, curtailment start/stop records, or measured flowgate relief were retrieved.
No public NERC TLR log for Message 105558 was retrieved at observation time.
No evidence ties this action to data-center backup generation, customer load shed, or the mandatory demand-response registrations in Messages 105561/105562.
No release or downgrade posting was present in the retrieved PJM page.

failures.detail: Transaction-level interchange tags and the completed TLR log were not available in the retrieved public posting.

rivalHypotheses: The TLR action reflects a real transmission constraint requiring reallocation after less consequential measures were exhausted.
The action is a bounded scheduling reallocation among firm transactions and may resolve without customer interruption, backup generation, or broader capacity scarcity.
The action may be driven by local or neighboring-system flow patterns rather than underperformance of the earlier demand-response dispatch.
